perf.s5.intro: `ecosystem.json` carries **{n_nodes} nodes / {n_edges} edges** ({n_seeds} seed entities, 5 chat exports, {n_ext} externals). Seed validation (an edge weight ≥ 3 into the seed evidences it):
perf.s5.relay: **The association operates as a relay.** Its channel is both a megaphone and a redistribution point: the association handle anchors **{assoc} mention weight** onto the association seed (post alias merge; 1,793 of them the channel's own post-signature handle), it has relayed the department's weekly seminar digests since 2018 — **{n_posts} all-time channel posts** (anchors {d0} → {d1}, outside the analysis window) — and **کوانتا (QuantaSC study circles) takes {q_pct} of the channel's forward weight** ({q_fwd} of {ch_fwd}), on top of {q_men} mention weight. The strongest subgroup partnership in the graph is thus the association's own spin-off study-circle network.
perf.s5.unverified: **Unverified seed caveat:** {labels} has zero forward and mention edges in the exports — an in-person gathering with no digital footprint, so every graph statement in this report is made over the {n} evidenced seeds only.
perf.s6.fixed.caveat: *Caveats (inherited from the extraction rules):* the mention count `n` includes **deadline-style times** (00:00 / 23:59 appear in several threads' `times` lists), so a mode is far more reliable than its n; and colloquial hour-only mentions such as «ساعت ۳» (old-style 15:00) are **never collected** — only literal HH:MM strings are, so evening events advertised colloquially are under-represented here.
perf.s6.intro: `mechanics` lists {n} recurring patterns ({n_fixed} fixed event slots, {n_peak} weekday peaks, {n_tx} ledger-linked hours; n ≥ 5 only).
perf.s6.night.para: The single strongest hourly signal in the corpus is late-night coordination: the private group's busiest hour is **23:00 with {priv23} messages** and the public group's is **00:00 with {pub0} messages** (its 23:00 follows at {pub23}). Between 22:00 and 01:00 the private group posts {priv_pct} of its volume and the public group {pub_pct} — student-run coordination happens after midnight, not in the 13:00–19:00 business band the fixed slots occupy.
perf.s6.ss.para: The dedicated summer-school channel ({n} in-window posts) runs its live sessions at a fixed class hour — **18:00–19:10** («{kw}» in the 1405 course calendar; event-hour 18:00 appears in {n_ev} posts, «همه‌روزه») — and publishes its announcements in a **Saturday slot**: {n_sat} of {n} posts sit in the شنبه weekday-slot peak.
perf.s6.tx.note: The 04:00 entry (n = 5) sits right at the n ≥ 5 threshold and reflects night-time bookkeeping posts — observational, not a scheduled mechanism.
perf.s7.event_ref: **event_ref is affiliation, not evidence.** The LLM attached explicit `event_ref` labels to **{aff} messages**, and the correlation stage added **{fb} keyword-fallback memberships** (first-6-keyword substring match) to reach {affiliated} affiliated messages across the 46 message-bearing threads. In fallback-heavy threads — e.g. `final-receipt-handover-1405` (1 explicit of 413) — the per-thread `n_messages` and `announcement_lag_days` are therefore approximate, and §4 marks them as such.
perf.s7.final: **Final state: {cls_pct} classified.** The LLM layer labeled **{llm} messages with `method=llm`** (confidence-gated at 0.7); after the Task-14 precision passes (risky-word corroboration, lexicon pruning, word-boundary matching for short keywords, demotion of low-confidence topical labels on micro-messages, multi-label gating on forwarded/channel broadcasts, affirmation-only resolution to meta_noise, verb-suffix boundary matching, and category blockers for macro-economy and external-journal markers), **{unlabeled} in-window messages** hold no label rather than a speculative one, and {unl} records remain unlabeled corpus-wide. **{decisions} messages** carry `is_decision` (all from the LLM layer).
perf.s7.further: **Further limitations.** meta_noise is the largest category ({noise} of {corpus} corpus labelings) — the groups are, by volume, mostly chat. Labels are multi-label (capped at 4): {multi} of {n} in-window messages carry more than one category, so category sums exceed message counts ({corpus} corpus labelings over {total} records). Service messages (joins, title changes, poll closes) are excluded from every narrative and histogram here. Timestamps are export-local (UTC+03:30) — hour patterns are Tehran-local.
perf.s7.intro: Three-layer pipeline over the {total} parsed records; the analysis denominator is the **{n} in-window, non-service messages**:
perf.s7.layer2: **Layer-2 coverage plateaued at {raw_pct} raw / {top_pct} topical** — {l2} of {n} messages received at least one lexicon/rule label, but only **{topical} carry at least one topical category** (anything beyond the chatter pair meta_noise/community_social); the remaining **{chatter} layer-2 labelings are classified-only-chatter**. The structural ceiling is visible in the data itself: {no_text} in-window messages have no text and no media to classify, {voice} are voice-only with no text, and {short} of the layer-3 messages are 15 characters or shorter — so the residue was routed to layer 3 rather than forced into topics.
